finding: `taskflow close --write` can exceed the caller timeout after it has already mutated the live ledger, updated the planning mirror, and created both target/planning commits, leaving the operator with no final JSON response and forcing manual triangulation to learn whether retrying would duplicate or corrupt closeback state.
expectedBehavior: Long close transactions should either complete within the default operator timeout, stream/checkpoint durable progress, or expose a first-class `taskflow close-status` / recovery receipt that tells the operator whether ledger close, target commit, and planning commit already landed.
evidenceOrRepro: ATM-GOV-0277: `node atm.mjs taskflow close --task ATM-GOV-0277 --actor codex-skl-captain --historical-delivery 0b0918c3bfc14d90a68b51738d0e5f433f895858 --write --json` timed out at the caller after about 34 seconds. Read-only follow-up showed live ledger status `done`, planning frontmatter `done`, framework close commit `2a7c4b4d6`, and 3KLife planning close commit `26b046b0` already existed. Manual `tasks status`, `git status`, and git log inspection were needed to avoid unsafe retry.
followUp: Add close transaction status receipts with phase markers (`ledger-written`, `target-commit-created`, `planning-commit-created`, `post-cleanup-complete`) and make timeout recovery diagnostics point to a safe read-only status command before retry.
